which.instructions: Which sentence of the author's text disagrees with the captured evidence? A disagreeing sentence asserts something the captured evidence, or the author's own figures elsewhere in the text, show to be otherwise.

criteria.S2: It retries once on a truncated draw; the budget covers both:
criteria.S4: Version 1.2 ships. e.g. the lower-case start stays joined.
criteria.S5: The gate runs first — before classify – and costs one call.
criteria.S12: A ninth sentence, with a clause, is here.
criteria.S13: A tenth sentence after a blank line.
criteria.NONE: No sentence disagrees with the evidence. Also false when: the evidence merely fails to establish the text; the capture does not touch what the text is about; the text says less than the evidence shows; the text describes what a design PROPOSES to build, which evidence captured beforehand cannot contradict; or the reader is simply uncertain. Insufficiency is not disagreement.

criteria.CURRENT: It describes the code, a tool's output or a measurement as it exists now — something the captured evidence could confirm or contradict.
criteria.PROPOSED: It describes what this design will build, add or change. Evidence captured before the design exists cannot contradict it.
criteria.ARGUMENT: It is reasoning, motivation, judgement or framing rather than a factual statement about the code.
